## October 10: When the Numbers Line Up

You know what I love about playoff baseball? When a 53% pick actually feels like a lock once the game starts playing out. The Guardians took care of business at home yesterday, and our model caught the edge just right. Days like this remind me why I still get up early to check the pitching matchups—even after all these years.

## Looking Ahead: October 11's Main Event

Now here's where it gets interesting. The Dodgers head to Milwaukee, and I've seen this storyline before—the big market powerhouse rolls into a smaller park where the home team just plays loose and hungry. Tarik Skubal's been lights out, no question. The guy's a horse. But Jacob Misiorowski at home in Milwaukee? That's a different animal.

Our model likes the Brewers at 61%, and I'm inclined to agree. Home field advantage in October isn't just about the crowd—it's about familiarity, routine, sleeping in your own bed. The little things that don't show up in the box score but absolutely show up in the ninth inning.

## The Matchup That Matters

Skubal's got the pedigree, but Misiorowski's got the ballpark knowledge and a bullpen that's been waiting for this moment all season. In my three decades covering this game, I've learned that October baseball rewards the team that believes they belong—not just the team with the better regular season résumé.

The Brewers are at home. They're confident. And that 61% edge? That's not just algorithm noise—that's a real, measurable advantage.

See you tomorrow when we see if the home cooking continues.
